study.question: Under the fixed four-task recipe, does feeding the first history retrieval back into both later field queries and history transformations improve click discrimination beyond an otherwise identical two-read architecture?
study.hypothesis: Observed baseline-din code conditions a single history pool on target-item fields and only subsequently combines it with context; it has no feedback path from retrieved history into further retrieval. Baseline click AUC is 0.6555440824, with empty/1-16/17-64/>64 history AUCs 0.5758203/0.6143212/0.6353650/0.6578031. These slices have different prevalence and cannot diagnose this bottleneck. The testable hypothesis is that an initial field-wise read disambiguates intent, and its feedback to the next query and affine history transformation improves a second read. This is an architectural hypothesis motivated by inspected information flow, not an empirically established explanation of slice gaps.

nearest_work.difference: Archived primary text lines 53-97 describes target-dependent local activation pooling. Retain sparse field embeddings and four-task adapted readout recipe but replace one pooled vector with field-wise repeated retrieval. Not an exact DIN reproduction.

Pinned benchmark code lines 158-282 repeatedly cross-reads history into non-sequential tokens and updates both using FFNs. Candidate uses shared reader projections, field-specific input projections, explicit strict masked normalization and one field-conditioned event write; no EST-specific heterogeneous FFN reproduction. This is a benchmark-code comparison, not an original EST paper audit.

Pinned benchmark code lines 123-219 and 275-313 has group/task hubs and affine broadcasts. Candidate retains the broad affine-conditioning idea but uses the mean of current field tokens to gate event-local updates between two direct field-to-history reads, without separate categorical/sequence/task hub sets. No claim that this is novel relative to INFNet.

Archived benchmark section 2.3 identifies OneTrans, EST and INFNet as layer-wise approaches. Candidate tests two feedback edges rather than reproducing any named full architecture. Original OneTrans/EST paper detail is unavailable through current primary-text references; novelty remains unverified.

inherited_components: FeatureEmbeddingDict with 16-dimensional embeddings and baseline source-based field enumeration
MultiTaskModel get_inputs, label order and probability dictionary API
Four separate 128/64 Dice task towers and default host sum of four BCEs
Target-only static fields plus masked history fields/action, never target action
General repeated cross-retrieval and affine-broadcast ideas from inspected pinned benchmark implementations; no model code copied from those implementations
study.proposed_difference: Implement event tokens by projecting concatenated visible item/action embeddings and a prefix-position scalar to width 32. Give each user/context/target field its own 16-to-32 projection. Let G1=FieldMix1(F0), R1=Read1(G1,E0), F1=G1+R1. Write E1=mask*(E0+local(LN(E0))*sigmoid(scale(mean(Cw)))+tanh(shift(mean(Cw)))), where Cw is F1 for w=1 or G1 for w=0. Let G2=FieldMix2(F1), Cq=F1 for q=1 or G1 for q=0, and F2=G2+Read2(Cq,E1). Flatten F2 with original static embeddings into unchanged-width task towers. Both binary factors change only whether first-read evidence reaches a conditioning destination; w=0 still transforms history using static field context. All four variants retain active write parameters and identical module sizes. Cross-attention explicitly zeros padding weights and handles empty histories. This is not full history self-attention or event-event temporal modeling; positions provide only relative visible-prefix order. It changes normalization, tokenization and readout versus DIN, so only the factorial controls attribute feedback.
predictions: Predeclared primary comparison: validation click AUC(exchange_q1_w1) minus click AUC(exchange_q0_w0). A gain >=0.0005 is the practical continuation target, not a significance threshold. Compare all four results against baseline-din separately.

Query effects are A11-A01 and A10-A00; write effects are A11-A10 and A01-A00. Positive effects in both settings support both paths. Interaction A11-A10-A01+A00 greater than zero suggests complementarity, but a single seed cannot establish it.

Joint feedback should be more consequential on nonempty histories. For empty histories R1=R2=0 and q/w choices are functionally irrelevant at fixed parameters; this is a host correctness invariant, not an expectation of equal trained empty-slice predictions.

Report all task AUC/logloss, auxiliary mean separately, and the existing predeclared history bins with sample, positive and negative counts. Other slices require authorized host availability and train-defined bins; missing diagnostics stay unavailable.

Architecture cost should avoid quadratic history-history attention: readers O(B*fields*history*32), field mixing O(B*fields^2*32), one linear-cost write. Report measured parameters, training/validation wall and allocated GPU seconds, examples, peak memory and model latency/throughput; no efficiency claim from FLOPs alone.
falsifiers: If neither feedback contrast improves click AUC and A11 is within or below A00, the current feedback implementation lacks support even if every architecture beats DIN.
If only one path helps, reject the need for both paths and retain the simpler supported path for follow-up. A nonpositive interaction rejects superadditivity, not all additive benefits.

If padding replacement changes predictions, all-empty histories yield nonfinite results, or masking changes cause invalid gradients, the implementation fails readiness; do not interpret its predictive result.

If quality gains disappear in paired seeds or require unacceptable measured cost under the fixed per-trial cap, do not claim robust improvement or efficiency. A failed single implementation does not refute all iterative interaction mechanisms.
alternative_explanations: DIN-to-candidate gains may come from softmax normalization, context-conditioned initial retrieval, field tokenization, raw-field skip, position features, capacity or tower input width rather than feedback.

Field-conditioned writes may act as generic nonlinear expansion rather than better historical evidence selection; static-write controls isolate history-derived conditioning, not every aspect of event updating.
Differences across history slices may reflect label prevalence, user mix, training frequency or auxiliary label semantics rather than information-flow bottlenecks.
One-pass optimization and random initialization can favor one architecture; shared parameter counts and paired host seed mitigate but do not eliminate this.
Offline historical feedback may be immature at prediction time; all conclusions apply only to the frozen official_offline benchmark.

cost_plan.estimate_ref: baseline-din: 328.9133 s wall, 297.2351 s train, 25.8242 s inference, 4,196,814,848 peak GPU bytes; runtime estimated_unit_seconds=481.3476, trial_cap_seconds=1203.36897. Budget at entry=170721.77 s. New architecture cost remains unmeasured.
cost_plan.attribution_reserve: Four full-data variants at the same paired seed; expected 350-800 s each, conservative maximum 4*1203.36897=4813.48 s if each reaches the cap. Count all host readiness checks, failures, diagnostics and retries. Reserve an additional 12000 s for two further paired seeds of supported candidate/closest control and baseline repeats when warranted; do not execute those in this proposal phase.
cost_plan.assessment_reserve: Reserve 20000 s plus host-dependent scoring overhead for final repetitions and assessment. No heldout access in this phase; freeze source/config/checkpoint hashes, selected models, closest controls, key ablations, seeds and commands before requesting closed assessment. Closed results never reenter open memory.
cost_plan.stop_rule: Do not train in the coding workspace. Syntax and AST checks only here; Torch is declared unavailable. Host must verify feature dimensions, four finite [B,1] outputs, default loss backward, both/all-empty histories, padding-value invariance, target-action invariance, event-write mask and identical parameter counts across the four configs before interpreting results. Test fixed-weight empty-history equality across configs and finite nonzero gradients on active paths. Reuse only the accepted baseline receipt with matching protocol/source hashes; raw parquet digests and loader readiness are frozen host prerequisites, not independently reverified here. Stop at trial cap, overall hard deadline, integrity failure, or when no discriminating full run plus assessment reserve fits. Never silently change batch size/history/precision or retry unknown execution. Record failed costs. No training/GPU performance or masking correctness is claimed by this proposal.
